# P2a UI static review — PASS

Reviewed current Source `8362e8ca7187164dc7d15173994528790f100368` against merged
P1 base `0d72037ca895893e8cf338d5ade8b37b1bb645b8`. This verdict covers independent
source review only. Full-app/native screenshots and all runtime gates remain
pending; no visual or runtime pass is claimed.

No blocking UI findings were found. The source change is confined to
`android_tools`: an additive module export, an official raw Gradle getter sidecar,
its decoder/binding, fixtures and attributed references. UI, project publication,
editor, tree and theme sources are unchanged. `project_model.rs`,
`generated_artifacts.rs`, `android_ui.rs` and `android_build.rs` are byte-equal to
the base; hashes are recorded in `ui-static.json`.

Basic and V2 consumers preserve their schemas. The new sidecar is decoded
separately against an immutable Basic model; missing/failed/malformed getter
facts return typed errors and cannot call a UI reset or replace Basic modules.
All individual getter invocations and the project catalogue have observed
available/unavailable wrappers. The shipping UI does not invoke the new decoder.
Authored tests cover optional/required getter failures, catalogue failures,
legacy Basic projection, nullable observations and stale model/selection binding;
all 28 are source-reviewed but were not executed by this reviewer.

Project and root names, public paths, reference identity paths and nullable Idea
names remain independent raw observations. There is no JVM fallback naming,
Rust collision rename, Kotlin facet guess or new tree display. The retained
Gradle and IntelliJ helpers demonstrate why raw names and later imported/internal
naming must stay separate. All six full reference files match their manifest
hashes and byte counts, with original Apache attribution retained.

The physical tree and raw model JSON in the Sync console remain explicitly
tracked in the retained module-presentation task report, lines 89–94. The new
sidecar also enlarges that existing console payload. Its filtering is a separate
tracked task; this review does not credit an improved tree or console, large
project responsiveness, or an Android Studio visual match.

Root still must verify current-source compilation and tests, real Gradle/SDK
captures, full app/native loading, empty/error states, resizing/focus and cleanup,
and full CI. Source isolation is not proof of actual Gradle API compatibility or
runtime serialization. No Cargo, rustc, Clippy, JVM, Gradle, SDK, native or app
command was run, and no repository or cache file was changed.
